the relationship between structure, function and evolution of tRNA(Glu).
the relationship between the structure of tRNA and its function, and the importance of this relationship to the cell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in vitro studies are useful for the design and analysis of RNA structure and function but do not necessarily translate to the in vivo environment.
the in vitro studies of tRNA(Glu) and tRNA(Gln), and the in vitro studies on the aptamers derived from them, have not been able to replicate the complexity of the in vivo system.
the in vivo system is very complex, and that in vitro studies cannot be directly extrapolated to in vivo studies, even for the same organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tRNA(Gln)-aptamer is nonfunctional in vivo, and the rationally designed mutant tRNA(Gin) is also nonfunctional in vivo.
in vitro and in vitro systems are not equivalent and that the results obtained from each system must be interpreted with caution.
in vitro selection of RNA aptamers is an important tool to understand the structure-function relationships of tRNAs, but it is not a substitute for in vivo studies.
